resources.string: No text could be read from this file.
Export the resume as a text PDF rather than as an image or a scan.
The pages are pictures, with no text behind them.
Export from the original document instead of scanning or screenshotting it.
The text comes out unreadable.
Re-export with fonts embedded, then open the file and check that the text copies out cleanly.
This file uses Type 3 fonts, which carry drawings instead of characters.
Re-export using an ordinary TrueType or OpenType font.
An embedded font could not be read.
Re-export from the original document with fonts embedded properly.
This file is larger than many application forms accept.
Keep it under 2.5 MB, usually by removing or shrinking images.
This file is encrypted.
Save an unprotected copy, with no password and no permissions restrictions.
This is an XFA form, so most software reads only the empty shell.
Print or export the form to a flat PDF before sending it.
This is a PDF Portfolio: the visible page is only a cover.
Send the resume itself rather than a portfolio wrapper.
This file contains form fields.
Flatten the form so the text is part of the page.
Some characters come out as question marks.
Re-export with fonts embedded, and check the text copies out cleanly.
Some glyphs have no meaning outside this file.
Replace icon fonts with plain text, then re-export.
Ligatures can drop letters out of words such as \"workflow\".
Turn off discretionary ligatures when exporting.
A font is referenced but not embedded.
Embed all fonts when exporting, so characters map the way you intended.
Words run together when the text is extracted.
Re-export from the original document rather than converting from another format.
Text is written one character at a time.
Avoid heavy letter-spacing effects, then re-export.
This file contains text drawn invisibly.
If it came from a scan, that is expected. Otherwise remove it; recruiters read it as keyword stuffing.
This file contains white-on-white text.
Delete it. Hidden keywords are treated as a deliberate attempt to game the search.
Very little text was recovered for this many pages.
Open the exported file and confirm you can select and copy every part of it.
Images cover most of the page.
Keep resume content as real text rather than as pictures of text.
Some text is rotated.
Lay the text out horizontally. Rotated runs are often dropped or misplaced.
A page is rotated.
Save the file with every page upright.
This is not a common resume page size.
Use A4 or US Letter so the layout survives being re-rendered.
This file has no accessibility tags.
Tags give software an explicit reading order. Enable them when exporting, if your tool offers it.
This file declares no language.
Set the document language when exporting.
This file is large for a resume.
Compress or remove large images to keep uploads quick.
Only the first pages were checked.
Nothing to fix. The remaining pages were simply not covered by this report.
This page is in columns, and the text extracts out of order.
Use a single column for anything that has to be read in sequence.
The order the text is stored in disagrees badly with the order it reads in.
Re-export from a single-column layout, then copy the text out and check it reads top to bottom.
Some lines are stored out of reading order.
Copy the text out of the exported file and read it through; fix anything that arrives in the wrong place.
A full-height gap splits this page into two columns.
Prefer a single column, or keep the side column to short, self-contained lists.
Content is laid out in a grid.
Replace tables with plain paragraphs and lists. Cells extract in storage order, not reading order.
Text sits in the header or footer area.
Move real content into the body of the page; some software discards the margins.
Your lines are packed very tightly.
Increase line spacing so two lines are not merged into one.
Your body text is very small.
Use at least 9pt.
This file uses a lot of different fonts.
Keep to two or three families. Each extra font is another chance for one to map badly.
Your margins are very narrow.
Leave at least half an inch around the page.
Some text falls outside the page.
Move all content inside the page boundaries and re-export.
Your bullets are drawn with unusual characters.
Use your editor\'s normal bullet list, so stray glyphs do not land mid-sentence.
This page is very densely packed.
Add some whitespace between sections so a person can skim it.
The same line repeats on every page.
Keep running heads short, or drop them. They repeat in the extracted text too.
No work-experience section was found.
Add a section headed \"Experience\" or \"Work Experience\". It is the field most systems rank on.
No conventional section headings were found.
Use plain headings such as \"Experience\", \"Education\" and \"Skills\".
Only one recognizable section heading was found.
Break the resume into the usual sections so it can be segmented.
No education section was found.
Add a section headed \"Education\". Many systems have a required education field.
No skills section was found.
List the tools and technologies you use. Recruiters search skills more than any other field.
Your headings look the same as your body text.
Make them visibly larger, bolder or capitalized.
Very few words were recovered for a resume.
Check the exported file contains everything you expect, and that all of it is selectable text.
No bullet lists were found.
Describe each role with short bullets. Solid paragraphs are harder to skim and to segment.
No lines look like a job title paired with an employer.
Write each role as a clear title and company line, with the dates alongside.
There is no summary paragraph.
Add two or three lines at the top describing what you do.
No email address was found.
Put a plain email address near the top of the first page. It is what most systems file you under.
No phone number was found.
Add one with its country code; some application forms require it before you can submit.
The top of the first page does not look like a name.
Start the resume with your name on its own line.
Your contact details are not on the first page.
Move your email and phone number to the top of page one.
Your email address is broken across pieces of text.
Write it as one uninterrupted piece, with no special spacing.
A link points somewhere other than the address it shows.
Make the visible text and the destination match.
More than one email address appears.
Keep a single address, so software does not have to guess which one to use.
There is no link to a profile, portfolio or repository.
Add one link that shows your work.
A web address is written without https://.
Write the full address so it is recognized as a link.
Your phone number is written in an unusual shape.
Use a plain international form, such as +1 555 010 1234.
No dates were found.
Give every role a period, such as \"Jan 2020 - Present\", so your timeline can be reconstructed.
Most entries have no dates.
Give every role and qualification a date range.
A date range is written in a form most software cannot read.
Use a recognized form such as \"Jan 2020 - Mar 2022\" or \"2020 - 2022\".
A date range ends before it starts.
Swap the start and end dates.
A date is in the future.
Correct the year, or write \"Present\" for ongoing work.
Your dates are written several different ways.
Pick one format and use it everywhere.
Nothing marks a role as ongoing.
Write \"Present\" as the end date of your current role.
A numeric date reads differently in different countries.
Spell the month, as in \"Mar 2022\".
Almost none of your bullets carry a number.
Add figures where you have them: volumes, percentages, timeframes, team sizes.
Most bullets open with filler rather than something you did.
Start each one with a concrete verb: built, led, reduced, migrated.
Your resume uses \"I\" and \"my\".
Drop the pronouns and start from the verb. That is the convention in most markets.
Some bullets run long.
Keep them to roughly two lines, so a skim-reader finishes them.
This resume is long.
Length is not a defect, and there is no universal one-page rule. Keep the pages that earn their place.
There is a gap between two dated roles.
A gap is not a problem. Add a one-line explanation if you want to; many strong resumes simply do not.
Long stretches are set in capitals.
Reserve capitals for short headings. They slow reading and can defeat case-sensitive search.
Many bullets start with the same phrase.
Vary the openings so the section does not read as boilerplate.
